info.title: canopy private-server
info.description: Admin/operator API for the canopy fleet manager. Requests are gated behind Tailscale auth; admin-only endpoints additionally check the caller is on the admin list.

200.description: The newest id in the supersedes chain rooted at the given id.
`true` if the caller's Tailscale identity is on the admin allow-list; `false` otherwise (including when no Tailscale identity is present).
Server-versions URL with embedded auth secret, if configured.

409.description: Another device already claims this node id.

503.description: Tailnet directory not configured or unreachable.

409.description: Both source and target hold tailscale identity or a server attachment.

post.summary:
Look up a Tailscale IP / node id / DNS name in the directory and
return the canonical identity if found. Used by the attach UI's
preview pane so the operator can confirm the resolved node before
hitting attach.

503.description: Tailnet directory not configured or unreachable.

Find or create a `Device` row for a Tailscale node id resolved
from the supplied identifier, and attach it to the server
(`servers.device_id`). Used when a server has no device yet (e.g.
an operator-imported server that hasn't reported in) and the
operator wants to bind it to a tailnet node without going through
the device admin page first.

post.summary:
Servers without a group, used by the Ungrouped tab. Returned alongside a
total count so the UI can show "(N ungrouped)" without a second fetch.

200.description: The caller's most recent SQL playground query, if any.
Whether the read-only SQL playground is configured.

post.summary:
Server group ids bucketed by their **highest-ranked member's** rank.
`ServerRank::Production` outranks `Clone`, `Demo`, `Test`, `Dev` in that
order. Groups whose members are all unranked don't appear in the response
at all (the status page intentionally hides them — they're typically dev
scratch).
post.description: Within each bucket, groups are ordered alphabetically by name.

200.description: Server group IDs grouped by highest-ranked member's rank.

has_range_override.description: If true, this ranged artifact has an exact-version override (only when is_exact=true)

is_exact.description: Whether this artifact is for the exact version (true) or via a range pattern (false)

is_used_in_public_api.description: If true, this is the artifact that will be served to public API clients

version_range_pattern.description: The version range pattern if this is a ranged artifact, None if exact

identifier.description:
Any of: a Tailscale CGNAT/ULA IP, a node id, or a DNS name —
the operator pastes whichever is most convenient from the
Tailscale admin console. The server resolves it via the
cached directory to the canonical `(node_id, name, tailnet)`
tuple before persisting.
Any of: a Tailscale CGNAT/ULA IP, a node id, or a DNS name.

slack_open_delay.description:
Optional initial value (seconds) for the group's Slack open
cooldown. Omit to let the database default apply.

tailscale_node_id.description:
The Tailscale node ID this device is attached to, if any. The
live IP / display name corresponding to this id is in
[`DeviceInfo::tailnet_live`].

oneOf.description:
Live snapshot from the Tailscale control plane for a device
that's currently attached by `tailscale_node_id`. `None` if the
device has no tailnet attachment, the directory isn't
configured, or the node id isn't in the directory's cache.

HealthState.description:
Server's self-reported health state, derived from the most
recent status row's `healthy` field and `health[]` array.
Orthogonal to [`ShortStatus`]: a server can be reachable
(`up`) and reporting itself unhealthy at the same time.

The UI renders this as the *border* of `<StatusDot>` so both
dimensions (reachability and self-report) show in one glyph.

HealthcheckSeverityData.description: Catalog row enriched with a `pending_review` flag for the UI.

pending_review.description:
`true` when no operator has confirmed this row yet
(`reviewed_at IS NULL`). The catalog UI surfaces these.

note_count.description: Combined: this incident's notes + notes on all contributing issues.

notification_held_until.description:
`Some(t)` when this incident's Slack `incident_open` notice is
still inside the per-group cooldown window (`deliver_after = t`,
not yet shipped, not given up). `None` once Slack has heard about
the incident — or the open was cancelled. Lets the UI distinguish
"open but quietly held" from "open and operators have been paged".

server_group_name.description:
Display name of the group this incident rolls up to. Empty string
only if the group has been deleted out from under the incident,
which shouldn't happen via the API.

incidents.description:
Distinct incidents this issue is or was attached to, most recent first.
Empty for issues that never crossed the threshold to join an incident.

resolved_reason.description:
The string stored in the DB; parses to `ResolvedReason` if valid.
Kept as String to round-trip any historical value.

server_group_id.description:
Group id the issue's server belongs to; `None` when ungrouped. Used
by the UI to offer group-scope actions (silence, etc.) without a
second fetch.

server_group_name.description:
Display name of the group the issue's server belongs to. `None` when
the server is ungrouped; the UI hides the group prefix in that case.

server_name.description: The issue's server name (may be null — fall back to `server_host`).

IssueIncidentLink.description:
Minimal incident reference attached to an issue, enough for the UI to
render a link and indicate open/closed status. See `Incident::for_issues`.

max_major.description:
First unaffected patch. NULL while open — open issues
implicitly cover every patch from `min` to the end of the minor.

source_id.description:
Device row to fold *into* the target — usually the
auto-discovered tailnet-only row.

target_id.description:
Device row that keeps existing — usually the existing mTLS
row that owns the device's server attachment and history.

ready.description:
`true` when the latest published patch in this minor is itself
ready. An old, since-fixed issue on an earlier patch doesn't
dim the whole minor.

alert_when_down_for.description:
Threshold in seconds for the reachability sweep to consider this
server down. Always positive; only consulted when `is_monitored`
is `true`. The default at creation is 600 (10 minutes).

group_name.description:
Display name of the group this server belongs to (denormalised so list
rows don't need to fetch the group separately). `None` if ungrouped.

oneOf.description:
Self-reported health from the most recent status row. Same `None`
vs. populated-default semantics as [`Self::up`].

is_monitored.description:
Whether canopy is actively watching this server. When `false`, the
reachability sweep skips it and its issues don't contribute to
incidents.

public_name.description:
Name this server appears under in the public mobile-app server list.
`None` means the server is not listed publicly.

oneOf.description:
Reachability of the server, derived from the most recent status row.
`None` when the endpoint that produced this row didn't batch-fetch
statuses (e.g. the cheap list/get endpoints); a populated value of
[`ShortStatus::Gone`] means "fetched and no status exists".

Page_SqlHistoryEntry.description:
Standard wrapper for paginated list responses. The total reflects the full
row count (not just the current page) so the frontend can render page
counts without a separate count fetch.

ProblemDetailsSchema.description:
Wire-shape mirror of [`problem_details::ProblemDetails`] for OpenAPI.

Every error response from the servers serializes to this RFC 7807 shape via
[`AppError`]'s `IntoResponse`. This struct exists so OpenAPI specs can
reference a concrete schema; nothing actually constructs values of this
type at runtime.

detail.description: Human-readable explanation specific to this occurrence.

status.description: HTTP status code generated by the origin server.

title.description: Short human-readable summary of the problem.

type.description: A URI reference identifying the problem type.

fix_version.description:
Semver of the version that contains the fix. Must be in the same
minor as the issue's `min` and strictly above it.

ResolvedReason.description:
Reason an issue or incident was resolved by a human.

Stored as text in Postgres, validated as this enum at the API layer.
Categories follow common operational practice (PagerDuty/Sentry/Opsgenie):

- `Fixed` — the underlying problem was addressed.
- `WontFix` — won't fix; not worth doing, or not actually a problem.
- `Expected` — known/expected behaviour (e.g. planned maintenance window).
- `Duplicate` — a duplicate of another issue.
- `Flapping` — too noisy; suppressed rather than fixed (often paired with
  a snooze).

supersedes.description:
When set, the saved snippet supersedes the snippet with this id (i.e.
it's an edit). When absent, a fresh snippet is created.

oneOf.description:
The group this server belongs to, with its notes/tags so the UI can
render the "Group" section without a second fetch. `None` when the
server is ungrouped.

siblings.description:
Other servers in the same group (excluding `server`). Empty when the
server is ungrouped or alone in its group. Each entry carries its
own `up` / `health` so the UI can render a status dot per sibling.

slack_open_delay.description:
How long an `incident_open` Slack notification waits in the outbox
before the drainer is allowed to ship it. A resolve that arrives
inside this window cancels the open outright (and skips its own
notification), so groups with chronic flap can crank this up to
keep Slack quiet without losing the underlying incident record.

ServerGroupCard.description:
Status-page card for a server group. Replaces the old per-central-server
card: each card now stands for a group of equal-level servers (no implicit
root). The card carries the headline name plus the per-member status dots
— version comes from the most recently-pushing member.

alert_when_down_for.description:
Threshold in seconds for the reachability sweep to consider this
server down. Always positive; only consulted when `is_monitored`
is `true`. The default at creation is 600 (10 minutes).

group_name.description:
Display name of the group this server belongs to (denormalised so list
rows don't need to fetch the group separately). `None` if ungrouped.

oneOf.description:
Self-reported health from the most recent status row. Same `None`
vs. populated-default semantics as [`Self::up`].

is_monitored.description:
Whether canopy is actively watching this server. When `false`, the
reachability sweep skips it and its issues don't contribute to
incidents.

public_name.description:
Name this server appears under in the public mobile-app server list.
`None` means the server is not listed publicly.

oneOf.description:
Reachability of the server, derived from the most recent status row.
`None` when the endpoint that produced this row didn't batch-fetch
statuses (e.g. the cheap list/get endpoints); a populated value of
[`ShortStatus::Gone`] means "fetched and no status exists".

health.description: Per-check breakdown from this push. `[]` for legacy rows.

healthy.description:
Server's overall self-reported health from this status push.
`true` for legacy rows that predate the contract.

Severity.description:
RFC 5424 syslog severities.

Stored as text in Postgres; validated as this enum at the API layer.
Default is `Error` (incidents only open at severity ≥ Error, so the
default is intentionally above the floor — most devices that bother
pushing an event mean it).

at.description:
When the snapshot should be "as of". Returns the most recent
status row with `created_at <= at`. Omit (or `null`) to get
the latest status (no time bound).

StatusSnapshotData.description:
What the UI needs to render a status snapshot — the curated
fields ServerDetail already shows (so the modal/section can look
like the rest of the app) plus the new `healthy` / `health` and
the raw `extra` blob for forward-compat as the contract expands.

last_seen.description:
When the Tailscale control plane last saw this node. `None` if
the API didn't carry a value (or it didn't parse).

online.description:
Derived: `last_seen` is within the last 5 minutes — Tailscale's
own "online" heuristic in the admin console. False when
`last_seen` is missing.

notes.description:
Optional operator notes. `None` leaves the existing notes alone…
well, actually it overwrites with NULL — pass the current value
to preserve. The UI sends the full current state.

ready.description:
`true` when this version has no unresolved known issues. See the
`version_known_issues` table and `add_known_issue`/`resolve_known_issue`
endpoints for management.
`true` when this version has no unresolved known issues.
